'''George Richard Pickett''' [[Royal Society|FRS]] (10 April 1939 – 21 July 2024) was a British physicist who was Professor of [[Cryogenics|Low Temperature Physics]] at [[Lancaster University]].<ref name="Who">{{Cite web|url-access=subscription|url=https://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540884.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-30829|title=Pickett, Prof. George Richard, Professor of Low Temperature Physics, University of Lancaster, 1988, now Distinguished Professor|website=WHO'S WHO & WHO WAS WHO|year=2007|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U30829|isbn=978-0-19-954088-4}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.physics.lancs.ac.uk/people/george-pickett|title=Professor George Pickett - Physics at Lancaster University|publisher=Physics.lancs.ac.uk|accessdate=6 October 2014}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Pickett was born on 10 April 1939. He was educated at [[Bedford Modern School]] and [[Magdalen College, Oxford]] (BA 1962; DPhil).<ref name="Who"/>

Pickett was a Lecturer, Senior Lecturer, Reader and then Head of the Department of Physics at [[Lancaster University]].<ref name="Who"/>  In the [[Nobel Prize|1996 Nobel Prize]] citation of [[physicist]] [[David Lee (physicist)|David Lee]], credit was given to Pickett and his research group for their work on [[Helium-3|<sup>3</sup>He]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lancaster.ac.uk/sci-tech/news/?article_id=2204 |title=Science and Technology at Lancaster University |publisher=Lancaster.ac.uk= |accessdate=6 October 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141008202857/http://www.lancaster.ac.uk/sci-tech/news/?article_id=2204 |archivedate=8 October 2014 }}</ref>

In 1988, Pickett was elected a member of the [[Finnish Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acadsci.fi/jasenet/ulkomaiset_jasenet.htm|title=Suomalainen Tiedeakatemia|publisher=Acadsci.fi|accessdate=6 October 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141009063143/http://www.acadsci.fi/jasenet/ulkomaiset_jasenet.htm|archivedate=9 October 2014}}</ref>  In 1997 he was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]]<ref name="Who"/> and in 2006 a foreign member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lancaster.ac.uk/sci-tech/news/000227/ |title=Science and Technology at Lancaster University - International Honour for Low Temperature Physicist |publisher=Lancaster.ac.uk |accessdate=6 October 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141008203002/http://www.lancaster.ac.uk/sci-tech/news/000227/ |archivedate=8 October 2014 }}</ref> In 1998 he was awarded the [[Simon Memorial Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iop.org/activity/groups/subject/lt/prize/page_44359.html |title=Simon Memorial Prize: past winners |publisher=IOP |accessdate=2016-12-15 |archive-date=20 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220180053/http://www.iop.org/activity/groups/subject/lt/prize/page_44359.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2023 he was awarded an honorary degree by the [[Slovak Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/news/slovak-academy-of-sciences-awards-honorary-degree-to-professor-george-pickett |title=Slovak Academy of Sciences awards honorary degree to Professor George Pickett |accessdate=2024-03-07}}</ref> He died in [[Lancaster, Lancashire]] on 21 July 2024, at the age of 85.<ref>{{cite news |title=George Pickett, physicist whose team achieved the lowest temperature ever recorded – obituary |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/obituaries/2024/08/13/prof-george-pickett-physics-lowest-temperature-obituary/ |access-date=13 August 2024 |publisher=The Telegraph |date=13 August 2024}}</ref>
